advances:
The displayed scalar calibration is not simultaneously convex-polytopally
realizable.  The obstruction occurs already in the three exact clips of the
middle polygon.  More generally, if
\[
g_i=x,\qquad g_\ell=y,\qquad g_q=1-x-y
\]
and all three closed caps \(K\cap\{g_j\geq0\}\) of a two-dimensional convex
polygon have positive area, then
\[
\sum_{j\in\{i,\ell,q\}}|K\cap\{g_j\geq0\}|>|K|.
\]
For the proposed values the left side is instead exactly
\[
\frac{107}{320}+\frac{107}{320}+\frac14
=\frac{147}{160}=|K|.
\]
Thus no middle polygon \(K\) exists.  In particular, no rational endpoint
polygons, shifts, support contacts, or facetwise compatible midpoint
containment can complete the calibration.  The missing coupling in the
round-100 scalar relaxation is the strict overlap surplus forced by convexity
when all three covering caps are positive.
author: r101_tail_calibration
proof:
The three clipping halfplanes cover the whole plane.  Indeed, if a point is
in neither \(\{x\geq0\}\) nor \(\{y\geq0\}\), then \(x<0\) and \(y<0\), so
\(x+y<0<1\) and the point lies in \(\{x+y\leq1\}\).  Equivalently, this is
the pointwise consequence of
\[
g_i+g_\ell+g_q=1.
\tag{2}
\]
Hence \(C_i\cup C_\ell\cup C_q=K\), and ordinary clipping multiplicity gives
\[
|C_i|+|C_\ell|+|C_q|-|K|
=\int_K\left(
\mathbf 1_{C_i}+\mathbf 1_{C_\ell}+\mathbf 1_{C_q}-1
\right).
\tag{3}
\]
The integrand is nonnegative everywhere.

Suppose for contradiction that equality holds in (1).  Equation (3) then
shows that the clipping multiplicity is one almost everywhere.  In
particular,
\[
|C_i\cap C_\ell|
=|C_i\cap C_q|
=|C_\ell\cap C_q|
=0.
\tag{4}
\]
This is an exact consequence of the three simultaneous clips, not a scalar
cap relaxation.

Because \(K\) is a two-dimensional polygon, its boundary is a finite union
of exposed edges and vertices and has area zero.  The three cutting lines
also have area zero.  By \(|C_i|>0\) and (4), one can therefore choose
\[
p_i=(x_i,y_i)\in\operatorname{int}K
\]
away from all exposed faces and cutting lines such that \(p_i\) belongs only
to \(C_i\).  Thus
\[
x_i>0,\qquad y_i<0,\qquad x_i+y_i>1.
\tag{5}
\]
Likewise, \(|C_\ell|>0\) permits a point
\[
p_\ell=(x_\ell,y_\ell)\in\operatorname{int}K
\]
belonging only to \(C_\ell\), so
\[
x_\ell<0,\qquad y_\ell>0,\qquad x_\ell+y_\ell>1.
\tag{6}
\]
For a rational polygon these points may, if desired, be chosen rational,
since the two sets specified by the strict inequalities in (5)-(6) are
nonempty open subsets of \(\mathbb R^2\).

Consider the segment
\[
z(t)=(1-t)p_i+tp_\ell,\qquad 0\leq t\leq1.
\tag{7}
\]
The interior of a convex body is convex, so \(z(t)\in\operatorname{int}K\)
for every \(t\).  Moreover, (5)-(6) imply
\[
x(z(t))+y(z(t))>1
\qquad(0\leq t\leq1).
\tag{8}
\]
Let
\[
\tau_y=\frac{-y_i}{y_\ell-y_i},
\qquad
\tau_x=\frac{x_i}{x_i-x_\ell}.
\tag{9}
\]
These are the unique parameters at which \(y(z(t))=0\) and \(x(z(t))=0\),
respectively.  At \(t=\tau_y\), equation (8) gives
\[
x(z(\tau_y))>1,
\]
so \(x\) has not yet reached zero and therefore
\[
\tau_y<\tau_x.
\tag{10}
\]
For every \(t\in(\tau_y,\tau_x)\) one has
\[
x(z(t))>0,\qquad y(z(t))>0.
\tag{11}
\]
Choose one such \(t\).  The point \(z(t)\) is in the interior of \(K\) and
satisfies both inequalities in (11) strictly.  A sufficiently small open
disk around it is therefore contained in
\[
K\cap\{x>0\}\cap\{y>0\}
\subseteq C_i\cap C_\ell.
\]
This gives \(|C_i\cap C_\ell|>0\), contradicting (4).  Geometrically,
equality in the clipping sum confines every pairwise cap contact to cutting
lines or exposed faces of \(K\), whereas convexity of the segment between
the two exclusive cap regions forces a strict pairwise-overlap point in
\(\operatorname{int}K\).  This proves (1).

For the round-101 calibration, direct exact arithmetic gives
\[
c_i+c_\ell+c_q
=\frac{107}{320}+\frac{107}{320}+\frac14
=\frac{294}{320}
=\frac{147}{160}
=k.
\tag{12}
\]
All three prescribed cap areas are positive, so (1) says that their sum
must be strictly larger than \(k\), contrary to (12).  Therefore the middle
polygon is already impossible.  The compatibility condition
\((A_0+A_2)/2\subseteq K\), its facet checks, the four endpoint cap clips,
the shifts, and the support requirements \(d_0=d_2=2\) cannot arise in one
simultaneous realization.
statement:
Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a compact two-dimensional convex polygon and
put
\[
C_i=K\cap\{x\geq0\},\qquad
C_\ell=K\cap\{y\geq0\},\qquad
C_q=K\cap\{x+y\leq1\}.
\]
If
\[
|C_i|>0,\qquad |C_\ell|>0,\qquad |C_q|>0,
\]
then
\[
|C_i|+|C_\ell|+|C_q|>|K|.
\tag{1}
\]
Consequently, there do not exist rational two-dimensional convex polygons
\(A_0,A_2,K\), rational shifts \(a_i,a_\ell\), or any support data satisfying
the prescribed common-plane calibration with
\[
|K|=\frac{147}{160},\qquad
c_i=c_\ell=\frac{107}{320},\qquad
c_q=\frac14.
\]
